series.title: The Father Showed Up
series.subtitle: Teacher’s Edition · December 2026 · Kids Inspiring Nation
series.tagline: God is our Father. He sent His Son. He has never been late.
series.summary: Thirty 10-minute guides for December 1–30. Each night: watch a short clip from the film Eight O’Clock (0:00–2:30), read and explain the Word (2:30–4:00), three teaching truths (4:00–7:00), a response (7:00–8:00), three prayers and a declaration (8:00–10:00). Scripture is from the King James Version.
series.safeguarding: Never ask a child to share their own family story in the group. If a child tells you someone is hurting them: thank them, believe them, do not question them in front of others, and follow your safeguarding procedure today. KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
series.declaration: GOD IS MY FATHER. HE KNOWS MY NAME. HE HAS NEVER BEEN LATE.

opener.title: To Every Child
opener.verse: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.
opener.note: Read this aloud on December 1, and again on any night a new child joins. It takes about two minutes. Read slowly.
text: “And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” — 2 Corinthians 6:18 (KJV)
This is for you. Yes, you.

Maybe your father is at home tonight, and you can hear him laughing in the next room. Maybe he lives far away, and you only hear his voice on the phone. Maybe you have never met him. Maybe he has died, and you miss him. Maybe he is at home, but home does not always feel safe. Maybe he said, “I am coming,” and he did not come.
Wherever your father is tonight, listen: you have a Father who is never late.

Before anybody held you, He knew you. Before anybody gave you a name, He knew your name. He made your eyes, your laugh and the way you walk. You are not a mistake. You are not too much, and you are not too little.

Every good father you have ever seen, a daddy who carries his child on his shoulders, a grandfather who prays, an uncle who keeps his word, is a small picture of Him. God is not a copy of a good father. Good fathers are a copy of Him. The Bible says every family in heaven and on earth is named after Him.
“the Father … Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named” — Ephesians 3:14–15 (KJV, excerpt)

He is never too busy for you. He does not forget your birthday. He does not get tired of your questions. And when the right time came, He did not send a message or send money through somebody. He sent His own Son, Jesus Christ. Jesus said that when you look at Him, you are looking at the Father.
“he that hath seen me hath seen the Father” — John 14:9 (KJV, excerpt)
If your father let you down, it was not your fault. Not one bit of it. And it is not the end of your story.
“When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.” — Psalm 27:10 (KJV)
If somebody is hurting you, that is not your fault either. Tell a safe adult, and keep telling until somebody listens.
So tonight, and every night this December, we will say it together:

days.title: The Father Who Is Never Late
days.verse: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
days.story: In the film, a boy remembers one Christmas Eve. His father wore a big steel watch and made a big promise: chicken by eight o’clock. His mother had only a pot of boiling water and prayer. Some of us know homes like that, full of promises and worry. Tonight we meet a Father who is never late.
days.word: Read Galatians 4:1–7 aloud. Paul says that before Christ came, we were like a young heir who will one day own everything, but for now lives under guardians, waiting for the day his father has chosen. Then comes the key phrase: “when the fulness of the time was come.” God chose the hour, and He kept it. He sent His Son, born of a woman like any other baby, so that we could be adopted and call God our Father. Children: God has never once been late, even when it felt like it. Fathers: God did not send excuses or another promise. He sent His own Son.

truths.title: Grown-Up Problems Are Not Your Fault
truths.body: Maybe your home has been full of big promises and very little money, like the home in the film. Maybe you have heard grown-ups worry about school fees, or waited for someone who said, “I will be there.” It was never your job to fix the money, keep the peace or make anyone keep their word. That is a grown-up’s job. If a grown-up did wrong in your house, it is never the child’s fault. God sees you, and He is not late.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son, Right On Time
truths.body: God is our Father, and He sent Jesus Christ, His Son. For thousands of years the world sat at a door, waiting for the promised Child. It looked late. It was not. At the hour He chose, the Father sent His only Son, born small in Bethlehem, so that every waiting child and every father who failed could call Him Father. People sometimes promise what they cannot give. God has never made a promise He could not keep.

truths.title: Come Back To The Father First
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you left, or stayed but were never really there, and a child sat up waiting. Perhaps you were the funny one for ten minutes at a time, and the rest of the time your family carried your troubles. Your child carried it. But the Father who is never late sent His Son for the child you hurt, and for you. The way back starts with coming back to Him. Do nothing grand tonight. Tell God the truth, and let Him begin.

response.child: Write one promise you are still waiting for. Under it, write: “My Father in heaven is never late.” Keep it somewhere safe.
response.father: Write your child’s age now, and their age when you stopped being there. Look at the gap. Make no big promise yet. Pray for your child by name.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, I give You my waiting. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, for me.
Father, I was not there when my child waited; thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, for my child and me.
Father, let every waiting child at KIN know they are seen.
days.declaration: My Father in heaven is never late.

days.title: When My Father Does Not Come Home
days.verse: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.
days.story: A father gave his small son a watch and a promise: “When this short hand touches eight, Daddy will be at that door.” The door did not open. So the boy stopped the watch, to keep the promise alive. Maybe you have waited at a door too. Tonight God says the LORD will take you up.
days.word: Read Psalm 27:7–14 aloud. David was a king and a soldier, yet here he cries out like a child, asking God not to turn away or leave him. In verse 10, look at the word “when”. David does not pretend fathers never leave. Some do. But the verse does not end with the one who left. It ends with the LORD. To “take up” a child is to lift him and hold him close. Children, God lifts you. Fathers, God takes up the child you left. The psalm ends: wait on the Lord. Waiting for God is not waiting at a door that never opens.

truths.title: You Do Not Have To Hold The Time Still
truths.body: The boy in the film stopped the watch because the truth was too heavy. Maybe you have stopped a watch of your own: stopped hoping, or crying, or telling anybody how you feel, so nobody could disappoint you again. You did it to stay safe, and God is not angry. But keeping anybody’s promise alive was never your job. Let the time move. You will not fall. Somebody is holding you.

truths.title: The Father Kept His Promise In Real Time
truths.body: God is our Father, and His promise was more than words. He sent Jesus Christ, His Son, to take us up. He did not stop the clock to make it look true. He kept it: Jesus was born at a real hour, in a real town. When little children were brought to Jesus, He took them up in His arms and blessed them (Mark 10:16). That is the Father’s heart.

truths.title: Say “Sorry” To The Father First
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you have tried to say “I am sorry” and could not find the words, or said it and went back to the old ways. Somewhere a child decided what your lateness meant: that you were a liar, or that it was their fault. One day your child may need to hear “sorry”. Say it first to your Father. He will not turn away. He sent His Son for men who did not come home. If your child is not safe with you, get help first.

response.child: Listen to a clock for one minute and count sixty ticks. Then say quietly: “The LORD will take me up.”
response.father: Write “I am sorry” on paper, and under it what you are sorry for. Pray over it. Keep it. Send nothing yet.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, I am tired of holding the time still. Please take me up. Thank You for Jesus, Your Son.
Father, I am sorry, and I say it to You first; thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ.
Father, lift up every child at KIN still waiting at a door.
days.declaration: The LORD will take me up.

days.title: God Sees The Years I Lost
days.verse: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
days.story: The boy stopped the watch at eight o’clock, and it stayed there for seven years. He grew taller; the watch never moved. When his friend asked the time, he still said, “Eight.” Some of us carry a year like that, a year when something stopped inside. God saw every one of those years.
days.word: Read Joel 2:21–27 aloud. Locusts are small, but they come in armies and can eat a whole farm in one afternoon. Joel saw it happen to God’s people: years of work and food, gone. A locust year is a year that was eaten up before anyone could enjoy it. Then God promised, “I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten.” He did not say those years never happened or did not matter. He counted them. Children, your lost years were real, and God saw them. Fathers, God does not turn the calendar back. He restores in His own way.

truths.title: God Counts The Years Too
truths.body: Maybe somebody took years from you, years when you should have been safe, laughing and looked after. Those years were real, and it was not your fault. Like the boy in the film with his stopped watch, you may have carried one sad hour for a long time. God saw every year. Not one Christmas, not one birthday, not one night of waiting was hidden from Him. He does not promise the same years back. He promises you Himself.

truths.title: The Father Restores By Sending His Son
truths.body: God is our Father, and He restores by sending Jesus Christ, His Son. The whole world had lost countless years to sin. God did not send a new calendar. He sent His only Son into those lost years, to give us a life the locusts cannot eat. Jesus said He came that we might have life more abundantly (John 10:10). God may not give back the lost years as they were. He gives us Himself.

truths.title: Count The Years Honestly
truths.body: Fathers, tonight God asks you one quiet question: how many years? Do not hurry past the answer. Do not say, “They were too young to notice.” They noticed. Count honestly: the birthdays, the Christmases, the first school uniform, the nights somebody else put your child to bed. You cannot buy those years back, and God does not ask you to pretend you can. Bring the number to the Father who sent His Son, and let Him begin.

response.child: Write down seven good things God has given you this year. Read them quietly to God. Keep the list.
response.father: On paper, answer the question: how many years? Beside it, write one thing you missed in each year. Pray over it.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask anyone to say how many years, or to share their family story.
prayers: Our Father, You saw every year I lost. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, to give me a life nobody can take.
Father, I cannot give the years back; thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, into lost years like mine.
Father, restore the lost years in our homes and at KIN.
days.declaration: God saw every year. He gives me Himself.

days.title: Learning To Say “Our Father”
days.verse: And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
days.story: At a church lunch, every child prayed the Lord’s Prayer together. One boy could not make his mouth say the first two words: “Our Father.” A kind man bent down to his eye level and asked his name. Maybe “Father” is a hard word for you too. Tonight we learn it again.
days.word: Read Galatians 4:4–7 aloud. God sent His Son so we could be adopted into His family. Then God sends “the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.” “Abba” is what a small child calls his daddy, a warm, close word. Verse 7 says you are no longer a servant but a son, and an heir. Children, if that word is stuck in you, His Son’s Spirit says it from inside you. Fathers, notice the order: “because ye are sons.” A man becomes a son of God before he can be a good father.

truths.title: The Word Still Belongs To God
truths.body: Maybe “father” is a hard word for you, because of a man who left, or one you have never met. God is not angry that the word is slow to come. Like the boy in the film, you can stand with praying people until you can say it yourself. When your mouth is stuck, the Spirit of His Son says it in your heart. The word is not spoiled because a man failed. It still belongs to God.

truths.title: The Son Gave Us His Own Word
truths.body: Jesus, the Son, had every right to call God “Father”. But when He taught His disciples to pray, He gave them two words first: “Our Father” (Matthew 6:9). God is our Father, and He sent Jesus Christ, His Son, so we could say it too. Then He sent the Spirit of His Son, so we could say it even on the nights when our mouths are stuck and our hearts are sore.

truths.title: Become A Son Before You Try To Be A Father
truths.body: Fathers, your children learned the word “father” from you: whatever you were, that is what it meant. Maybe you cannot say “Our Father” either, because nobody showed you what it means. Before you can be a good father, you must become a son. God sent His Son so men like you could become sons of God. If you cannot say it yet, sit with people who pray, and listen. The children are saying the words you need.

response.child: Say “Our Father” slowly and quietly, three times. If it is hard tonight, just listen while others say it.
response.father: Say the two words out loud, once, slowly. Then pray the whole prayer. If you cannot finish, start with the first two words.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story, and never make a child say “Father” aloud.
prayers: Our Father, those two words are hard for me. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, to help me say them.
Father, nobody taught me this word; thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, so I can become Your son.
Father, teach every child at KIN to say “Our Father” and mean it.
days.declaration: God is my Father. I am His child.

days.title: My Father Gives Good Gifts
days.verse: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
days.story: A boy heard there was free rice with meat, so he came for the food. He found hungry children sharing their plates, and a girl serving others before herself. Maybe you came to church for the wrong reason too. That is all right. Tonight we meet a Father who gives good gifts.
days.word: Read Matthew 7:7–11 aloud. Jesus tells us to ask, seek and knock, and then He speaks to ordinary fathers. If your son asks for bread, will you give him a stone? If he asks for fish, will you give him a snake? Of course not. Even a man who has done wrong knows to give his child bread. Then the key words: “how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things”. Children, God is kinder than the kindest person you know. Fathers, ordinary gifts, given every day, make a father.

truths.title: God Is Not Like The People Who Failed You
truths.body: Maybe the grown-ups around you have not given you good things, so you hold your food tight and expect nothing. That does not tell you what God is like. Even ordinary people know how to give good gifts; how much more your Father in heaven. If you came to God for the wrong reason, as the boy in the film came for the meat, that is all right. God will not send you away.

truths.title: The Father’s Best Gift Was His Son
truths.body: God is our Father, and His best gift was not a thing: not money, or rice, or meat on a plate. It was His own Son. God so loved the world that He gave His only Son, Jesus Christ (John 3:16). He did not hand us something. He handed us Someone. We come hungry for many things, and He gives far more than we came for: His Son.

truths.title: Be Ordinary, Every Day
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you think you have nothing to give, so you give nothing. Or you dream of one big gift that will make up for everything. But the gifts that make a father are mostly ordinary: bread on the table, a school fee paid, time at bedtime, a promise kept, a word of blessing. Jesus said even imperfect fathers know how to give good gifts. Do not try to buy back the years with one big gift. Receive God’s gift, His Son, first. Then give, every day.

response.child: Quietly thank God for one person who shared with you this year. Tomorrow, if you want to, share something small.
response.father: If you live with your child, give one ordinary good thing tonight: bread, your time. If you are far from your child, feed a hungry person and pray for your child by name.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story. If a child seems hungry, arrange food quietly.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for people who share with me, and most of all for Jesus, Your Son.
Father, my hands are empty; thank You for Your Son, Jesus Christ. Teach me to give ordinary good things.
Father, make KIN a place where nobody hungry is sent away.
days.declaration: My Father in heaven gives good gifts.

days.title: God Keeps His Promises
days.verse: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
days.story: A man promised a group of children, “Every night. I’ll be here.” One boy had heard promises before. “People always say that,” he said. Maybe you feel the same, because promises have been broken in your life. Tonight we learn about the one Father who has never broken His word.
days.word: Read Lamentations 3:19–26 aloud. The man who wrote this sat in a city burnt to the ground. Everything was broken, and he remembered all of it. And still he wrote: “his compassions fail not.” Faithfulness means keeping your word, night after night, morning after morning. God’s mercies do not run out by evening; they are new again when the sun comes up. Children, you can count God’s mercies one at a time: every new morning is one more. Fathers, notice whose faithfulness this is: the LORD’s, not ours. Lean on His faithfulness before you try to keep your own promises.

truths.title: You May Count, And God Is Not Afraid
truths.body: Maybe, like the boy in the film, you are waiting for somebody to break their promise, because somebody always has. That is not wrong; when you have been hurt, it is wise to watch. Nobody can make you trust a grown-up who has not earned it. But you can test God. Count His mercies: one morning, one meal, one safe person. You will run out of nights before He runs out of faithfulness.

truths.title: God Promised A Son, And Sent Him
truths.body: A good leader who keeps showing up is only a small picture of a faithfulness that belongs to God. God our Father promised the world a Saviour and kept that promise through thousands of years. When the time was full, He sent Jesus Christ, His Son, not one minute late. People’s promises can be thin. God’s promise was His own Son, and He has never stopped meaning it.

truths.title: One Promise, One Night At A Time
truths.body: Fathers, if your promises have been broken before, do not make your child a big new one tonight; they have heard those before. Make one small promise before God, one you can really keep, and keep it one night at a time, leaning on the Father who sent His Son on time. Trust is rebuilt slowly, by promises kept, not by promises made. If your child is not safe with you, the first promise is: get help.

response.child: Start a secret count of God’s faithfulness. Each night this month, make one mark for one good thing God did.
response.father: Make one small promise you can really keep, and say it out loud to God. When you have kept it, mark it. Repeat tomorrow.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children whose promises have been broken at home.
prayers: Our Father, people have broken promises to me, but You never have. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son.
Father, my promises have not been worth much; thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, right on time.
Father, make KIN a place where promises are always kept.
days.declaration: God keeps His promises. He sent His Son.

days.title: You Can Talk To God Tonight
days.verse: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
days.story: In the film, a boy’s mother had stopped praying, so he tried for himself: “God. Good evening. It’s me.” No beautiful words, only the truth. Maybe you have never prayed, or you stopped long ago. Tonight you can begin the same way, and God will hear you.
days.word: Read Hebrews 7:23–28 aloud. In the Old Testament, priests stood between God and the people and prayed for them, but each one grew old and died. Jesus lives for ever. “Intercession” means speaking to God for someone else. So “he ever liveth to make intercession for them” means Jesus is speaking to the Father right now for everyone who comes to God by Him. “To the uttermost” means completely, all the way. Children, you do not need perfect words. Fathers, you do not need to be worthy first. Come to God through Jesus.

truths.title: You Can Start With “Good Evening.”
truths.body: The boy’s first prayer in the film was not fancy. It began like a boy greeting a neighbour, and it was heard. You can start the same way: “God. Good evening. It’s me,” and say your name. Tell Him the truth, even the hard parts: what you are afraid of, what you wish for, who you miss. On nights when you are too tired or sad to pray at all, remember: Jesus is still praying for you. You are not keeping the fire burning alone.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son To Be The Way In
truths.body: We can pray because God is our Father, and He sent Jesus Christ, His Son, who died for our sins, rose again, and lives to pray for all who come to God by Him. You are not alone when you kneel. Before you find one word, the Son is already speaking to the Father for you. Prayer is not a test you can fail. It is more like breathing: you do not need beautiful words to breathe. Just breathe, and come through Jesus.

truths.title: Say Whatever Is True
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you can talk your way past landlords and police officers, but you have never once talked to God. Perhaps you knelt once, felt foolish and got up. Nobody ever knelt beside you and showed you how. Start here: say whatever is true. Tell God your name, what you did, and that you cannot find the first word. You do not have to be worthy; that is why the Father sent His Son. Your prayer need not be good. It must be true.

response.child: Before you sleep, whisper one sentence: “God. Good evening. It’s me,” and say your name. Nobody else needs to hear.
response.father: Kneel or sit wherever you are and say one true sentence to God out loud. If you cannot find the first word, say that.

days.teacherNote: Pause for 20 seconds of silent prayer. Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: God. Good evening. It’s me. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, who prays for me when I cannot. Amen.
Father in heaven, I am a man who did not come home. Hear me because of Your Son, Jesus Christ. Amen.
Father, make our homes and KIN places where children learn to pray in their own words.
days.declaration: Jesus is praying for me tonight.

days.title: I Do Not Need To Pretend
days.verse: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
days.story: A boy told his class his father was a pilot and a doctor who lives in “Americanada”. Another boy asked, “Is that why he flew away?” and the class laughed. Maybe you have told a bigger story to cover an empty place. Tonight God says: with Me, you do not need to pretend.
days.word: Read Proverbs 22:1–6 aloud. Proverbs is a book of wise sayings, many written like a father teaching his son. A “name” here means your character: what others can trust about you. “Loving favour” means being truly trusted and loved. Riches can be lost, and silver and gold can be spent, but a good name lasts. It is not invented in one speech or one boast. It is “chosen” and built, one true sentence at a time. Verse 6 reminds fathers that children are trained by what we do, not only by what we say.

truths.title: You Do Not Need To Make Your Story Bigger
truths.body: Maybe you have said, “My father is…” and finished with something untrue: travelling, busy, rich, important. Like the boy in the film, you were covering an empty place, and that is understandable. But you do not need to lie to be worth something, and your real story is not too ugly for God. If somebody laughs at your family, that is unkind and it is not your fault. Walk away, and tell a safe adult. God knows your true story, and He loves you in it.

truths.title: The Father Sent A Real Son, Not A Story
truths.body: God our Father did not send a nicer picture of Himself. He sent His own Son, Jesus Christ, into a real family, a real town and real trouble. Jesus was born where animals eat and grew up in a village people laughed at. He came into real stories like yours, empty places and all. He did not come to the story you tell about yourself. He came to you, the real you, and He is not ashamed to call you His family (Hebrews 2:11).

truths.title: The Way Back Starts With A True Sentence
truths.body: Fathers, listen to what you say about your children when they are not there. Perhaps you have said “doing very well” about a child you have not seen in years. Your child may be covering the same empty place with a story about you. The way back starts not with a better story but with a true one. Tell God tonight: “I do not know where my child goes to school. I was not there.” He already knows. He is waiting for you to stop pretending.

response.child: Write one true sentence about your family that you have never said out loud. You do not have to show anybody. Give it to God.
response.father: Write three things you truly know about your child, and three things you do not. Pray over the second list, line by line.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group. If a child is teased about their family, speak with them privately afterwards.
prayers: Our Father, You know my real story; I do not have to make it bigger. Thank You for sending Jesus into my real life. Amen.
Father in heaven, I have told stories about my child. Thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, into the truth. Amen.
Father, make our homes and KIN places where every family’s true story is safe.
days.declaration: I do not need a story. I have a Father.

days.title: When Nobody Comes For Me
days.verse: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
days.story: The head teacher said, “Tomorrow, come with your father.” But nobody came for the boy. Then one man walked in and said, “I am here for him.” Maybe you have waited for somebody who never came. Tonight hear this: God has not left you waiting. He has come for you.
days.word: Read Psalm 68:3–6 aloud. David calls God’s people to sing and rejoice. A “judge of the widows” is a defender of widows, someone who stands up for them. “His holy habitation” is the high place where God lives. Yet this high God cares for the people at the bottom, and verse 6 says He sets lonely people in families. This is no excuse for any father to stay away. It is God’s own promise to every child who has waited for somebody who did not come: God Himself is a Father to you.

truths.title: You Are Not The Child Nobody Came For
truths.body: Maybe everybody else had somebody and you had nobody, at a school meeting, a prize-giving or a hospital bed. That emptiness was real, and it was not your fault. A child cannot make a grown-up come. But God calls Himself a father of the fatherless. He often sends people to stand in the doorway: a teacher, an aunty, a grandmother, a pastor. Let the safe ones stay close. If anybody is hurting you, tell one of them.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son To The Doorway
truths.body: In the film, one man walked in and said, “I am here for him.” But even a good man can only point to Someone greater. God is our Father, and He answered every empty doorway. He saw a world of children waiting outside closed offices and did not send a letter. He sent His own Son, Jesus Christ, to come Himself, and to say over each of us: I am here for him. I am here for her.

truths.title: It Can Stop With You
truths.body: Fathers, maybe you were the boy left waiting on the bench, and you learned to be funny, or hard, or busy instead. That explains a lot. It does not excuse it. But the Father sent His Son for the boy on the bench before He asked anything of the man you are now. The pattern of not coming can stop with you. Start by being where you promised to be. If your child is not safe with you, coming starts with getting help.

response.child: Write down the names of people who have shown up for you this year, even once. Quietly thank God for each one.
response.father: Write the name of the man who did not come for you. Under it write: “My Father in heaven sent His Son for me.” Pray for your child by name.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group. If a child seems troubled, speak with them gently afterwards, where another safe adult can see you.
prayers: Our Father, sometimes I feel nobody is coming for me. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, for me. Amen.
Father in heaven, nobody came for me, and I did not come for my child. You sent Your Son, Jesus Christ, for us both. Let it stop with me. Amen.
Father, make our homes and KIN doorways where no child waits alone.
days.declaration: Somebody has come for me. His name is Jesus.

days.title: I Do Not Have To Become Him
days.verse: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
days.story: A boy said quietly about his father, “I am just like him.” Coach T answered, “A good name is not what your father left you. It is what your Father calls you.” Maybe you are afraid of becoming the one who hurt you. Tonight God says: in Christ, you can be made new.
days.word: Read 2 Corinthians 5:14–18 aloud. Paul says that because Jesus died and rose again, those who belong to Him no longer live only for themselves. “In Christ” means joined to Jesus, belonging to Him like a child in a family. “A new creature” means something truly new made by God, not a patch on the old. “Old things are passed away” does not mean we pretend nothing happened; it means the old does not get the last word. Your face may stay the same. Your Father, your family line and your future can change.

truths.title: You Do Not Have To Become The One Who Hurt You
truths.body: Maybe somebody has said, “You are just like your father.” Maybe, like the boy in the film, you have said it yourself. His wrongs are not your name: “The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father” (Ezekiel 18:20). That goes for daughters too. When your hands go hot, stop, walk away and tell a safe adult. If somebody’s anger at home is hurting you, that is not your fault, and it is not your job to fix.

truths.title: See Jesus, And You Have Seen The Father
truths.body: How can we be new when the face in the mirror stays the same? God our Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ, so that we could be born into a new family. You need not guess what your new Father is like. Jesus said, “he that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (John 14:9). Look at Jesus: kind, truthful, patient, faithful. He shows you the Father who matters now, not the man in the mirror.

truths.title: You Cannot Change Your Face, But You Can Change Your Father
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you see your own father’s face in the mirror. You promised never to be him, and then you were. Do not lie to yourself about what you did. But in Christ you can be a new creature. Let the Father who sent His Son start a new line in your family, with you. If you are still dangerous when angry, get help before you go near your child.

response.child: Look in a mirror, on your own, and say quietly: “I am not my father’s mistakes. My Father in heaven calls me His child.”
response.father: Write one thing your father did that you have also done, and ask Jesus to start the new thing there. If it is anger, tell a pastor or counsellor this week.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group. If a child says someone at home is hurting them, follow your safeguarding procedure.
prayers: Our Father, I am afraid of becoming like the one who hurt me. Make me new in Jesus Christ, Your Son. Amen.
Father in heaven, I have done what my father did. I am sorry. Begin something new in my family, starting with me. Amen.
Father, let a new line begin in every home here tonight.
days.declaration: I am not my father’s mistakes. I am God’s child.

days.title: New Hands For A Hungry Heart
days.verse: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.
days.story: Forty-two pieces had become forty-one, and a boy’s hand was the reason. Coach T did not shout. He asked, “When does the hand start itching?” Then he said, “You are not a thief. You are a boy with a hungry habit.” Tonight God offers your hands a new job too.
days.word: Read Ephesians 4:22–29 aloud. Paul tells new Christians to take off the old life like old clothes: lying, lasting anger, stealing, unkind words. Then he tells them to put on the new life God gives. Look at verse 28. It does not stop at “steal no more”. It gives the same hands a new job: honest work, “the thing which is good”, so that they can give to someone in need. Stopping is only half of it. God does not just tie up a taking hand; He turns it into a giving hand. That is a promise of change, not only a rule.

truths.title: You Are Not A Thief; You Have A Hungry Habit
truths.body: Maybe your hand itches too: food, money, things from other children’s bags. It is still wrong, and you can stop. Ask the question from the film: when does my hand start itching? When I am hungry? When grown-ups worry about money? Fixing the money at home is not your job. If you are hungry or frightened about rent, tell a safe adult. Then give your hands a new job: help, serve, share.

truths.title: The Father Sent A Son With Real Hands
truths.body: How does a hand get a new job? Not by trying harder alone. God our Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ, with real hands. Jesus worked as a carpenter, touched people nobody would touch, broke bread and gave it away. At the end His hands opened wide on a cross, giving everything, for people with itching hands. In His Son, the Father gives us new hearts and giving hands.

truths.title: Name The Hour Your Hand Itches
truths.body: Fathers, when does your hand start itching? Payday? The betting stand? The friends who drink after work? Every man who has wasted what his children needed has an answer. Name yours; a cue you can name is a cue you can see coming. Give your hand a new job before the itch comes. Decide where you will be at that hour and where the money will go first. Tell one faithful man the truth, and let him ask you about it.

response.child: Choose one good job for your hands tomorrow: wash a plate, carry a bag, share a snack. Do it before anybody asks.
response.father: Write down the hour, the place and the feeling when your hand starts itching, and what it will do instead. Tell one faithful man.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group. If a child tells you privately there is no food at home, follow it up today.
prayers: Our Father, give my itching hands a new job. Thank You for Jesus, Your Son, whose hands give. Amen.
Father in heaven, my hand has taken what my children needed. Thank You for Your Son, Jesus Christ, whose hands gave everything. Amen.
Father, make our homes and KIN places where hungry hands learn to give.
days.declaration: My hands have a new job.

days.title: You Cannot Earn His Love
days.verse: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
days.story: A boy brought back money he had taken. Coach T only said, “Thank you for the change.” He had known all along, and he never used it against the boy. Tonight we meet the Father who loves us like that and more: He loved us before we made anything right.
days.word: Read Romans 5:6–11 aloud. People will hardly die even for a righteous man, Paul says, but Christ died for us while we were weak and in the wrong. “Commendeth” means proves, puts on display. Notice “while we were yet sinners”: not after we fixed ourselves or brought back what we took. God’s love came first. Verse 10 says we were like enemies, and still God made peace with us through the death of His Son. Children, He does not love you less when you do wrong. Fathers, you come back loved, not paid up.

truths.title: You Do Not Have To Earn His Love
truths.body: Maybe you have taken something, and you carry it like a stone: “If anybody finds out, they will never love me again.” God already knows, and He sent Jesus for you while you were still carrying it. You do not give it back so that He will love you. You give it back because He already does. Like the boy in the film, put it back, with a safe adult’s help if you need it. Then put the stone down.

truths.title: The Father Moved First
truths.body: Look at the order in Romans 5:8. God our Father did not wait for us to return what we took or to become good. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, first, to die for us while the money was still in our pockets. He knows everything you have taken and everything you have done, and in Christ He does not use it against you. His Son paid. Our turning back is the answer to His love, never the price of it.

truths.title: You Cannot Buy Your Way Back
truths.body: Fathers, you cannot buy your way back to your child with one big gift at Christmas. Children know the difference between being loved and being paid. Do one clean thing, with nobody clapping. Give back what is not yours. Tell the truth about a small thing. Then another. Trust is rebuilt slowly, and that is right. Remember: while you were still far away and in the wrong, the Father sent His Son for you.

response.child: If you have something that is not yours, plan to give it back this week, with a safe adult’s help. Thank God He loved you first.
response.father: Do one honest thing tomorrow that nobody will see or thank you for. Then thank God for sending His Son before you did anything.

days.teacherNote: Pause for 20 seconds of quiet. Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, You know all I have done and still love me. Thank You for sending Jesus, Your Son, before I was good. Amen.
Father in heaven, Your Son, Jesus Christ, died for me while I was still a sinner. Teach me one clean thing at a time. Amen.
Father, make our homes and KIN tables where love comes first.
days.declaration: God loved me first, before I was good.

days.title: My Father Calls Me His Child
days.verse: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
days.story: A boy’s test came back covered in red, with a name that stung: olodo, dunce. Then Coach T said, “In this place we don’t have olodo,” and gave him a new name, and the boy laughed. Maybe somebody has called you a name that stuck. Tonight, hear what your Father in heaven calls you.
days.word: Read 1 John 3:1–3 aloud. John begins with “Behold”: stop and look. Look at what kind of love this is. The Father does not only put up with us; He calls us His own children, sons and daughters. That is not a name we earn with good marks or good behaviour. It is a gift of His love. The world does not know us, John says, because it did not know Jesus either, so people may still call us by the wrong name. Children, the names people call you are not the last word. Fathers, you too were given a name you did not earn. Now learn your own child’s.

truths.title: A Red Number Is Not Your Name
truths.body: Maybe somebody called you a name that stuck: olodo, useless, dull. Maybe it came with a red mark on your test, like the boy in the film. A red number reports one test on one day. It is not a report on you. Being behind is not being foolish, and needing help is no shame. Ask for help with reading and sums, and keep asking. The Father who made you knows the gifts He put in you, even the ones nobody has found yet.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son So You Could Carry His Name
truths.body: God the Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ. The Son of God was born as a child, so that children like you could be called the children of God. He did not send a certificate. He sent His own Son and made a way into His family. When the world calls you olodo, or nobody, it does not know whose you are. Your Father knows. Christmas is His word to the world: my joy has come.

truths.title: Want To Know Your Child
truths.body: Fathers, do you know if your child can read? What makes them laugh? What names they are called at school? Many fathers boast about a child they hardly know. If you do not know, do not pretend. Your child does not need a father who knows everything, but one who wants to learn. Pray for your child by name. Then learn to speak good words over them, from a Father who has always spoken better things over you.

response.child: Write your name at the top of a page. Under it, write: “My Father calls me His child.” Keep it for yourself.
response.father: Write three questions you would ask your child if you could ask only three. Do not send them. Pray over each.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story, or names they have been called.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for calling me Your child, and for sending Jesus so I could be in Your family.
Father, thank You for calling me Your son through Jesus Christ, Your Son; teach me to know my child.
Father, make KIN a place where every child hears their true name.
days.declaration: My Father calls me His child.

days.title: My Scars Are Not My Name
days.verse: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
days.story: At night, in the rain, Coach T sat with a boy who has a small mark on his forehead. He told him that when Jesus rose, He kept His scars, and He is not ashamed of yours. Many of us carry marks, outside or inside. Tonight God speaks to them.
days.word: Read Isaiah 53:3–6 aloud. Isaiah wrote this hundreds of years before Jesus was born, about a Servant whom people would despise and turn away from. Christians have always seen Jesus here. “Transgressions” and “iniquities” are the wrong things we have done. “Stripes” are wounds. The Servant carried what was not His to carry: our sorrow, our sin, our shame. Children, Jesus knows what wounds feel like, inside and outside, and He came to heal yours. Fathers, whatever wrong you have done has a real name, and Jesus carried it so you could be forgiven.

truths.title: Your Marks Do Not Make You Less
truths.body: Maybe you carry a mark too: outside, where people can see it, or inside, where nobody can. Maybe you hide it, or feel ashamed of it. Hear this: a scar is not a sign that you are worth less. A scar is the place where a wound closed. It says you came through something, and that healing has begun. You do not have to cover your face or walk with your head down. Your scar is part of your story. It is not your name, and it is never the last word on you.

truths.title: Shame Explains, It Never Excuses
truths.body: The boy in the film said his father was ashamed. Fathers, shame can explain why a man hides, goes silent, makes excuses or stays away for years. It never excuses it. Shame says, “Hide.” God says, “Come.” Jesus took the shame of the cross on Himself (Hebrews 12:2), so you do not have to keep hiding. Bring what you did to God by its real name. Do not tell your child it was not that bad, or ask them to say it is all right. Then let someone help you change: a pastor, a counsellor, honest men.

truths.title: The Father Sent A Son Who Kept His Scars
truths.body: God the Father did not stay far from our wounds. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, and Jesus let Himself be wounded. His wounds were for those who did wrong, so they could be forgiven, and for those who were hurt, so they could be healed. When He rose, He could have come back without one mark on Him. He kept the marks of the nails and showed them to Thomas (John 20:27). He is not ashamed of your scars, and He turns away nobody who comes to Him.

response.child: Put your hand on your heart and say quietly: “My scar is not my name.”
response.father: Tell God one thing you have done that you have never said aloud. Write down the name of one person who could help you change.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story. Say slowly: “If somebody is hurting you, it is not your fault. Tell a safe adult.”
prayers: Our Father, thank You that Jesus is not ashamed of my scars; heal me where I hurt.
Father, thank You that Your Son, Jesus Christ, was wounded for my transgressions. Take away my shame and make me a father my children can trust.
Father, make our homes and our church places where every scar is met with kindness.
days.declaration: My scar is not my name.

days.title: Healing For The Wounded Heart
days.verse: When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole?
days.story: Coach T said that Jesus once asked a sick man one question. Then he said something worth remembering: some of us have carried the wound so long that it has become our name. Tonight we read that question together, and Jesus asks it of you.
days.word: Read John 5:1–9 aloud. Sick people lay round the pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, waiting for the water to move. One man had been ill thirty-eight years, and nobody would carry him to the water. Jesus saw him, knew how long, and asked one question. “Whole” means well all the way through: body, heart and life. Children, He asks you gently too, and “yes” or “I don’t know” are honest answers. Fathers, He does not ask whether you wish things were different. He asks whether you want to be made whole.

truths.title: Your Wound Is Not Your Name
truths.body: Maybe people call you by your wound: the one whose father left, the quiet one, the one who always fights. Maybe you have started calling yourself that too. Jesus sees how long you have carried it, and He asks you gently: do you want to be made whole? “Yes” is enough. “I don’t know” is honest too. And if a grown-up or a habit is hurting you, tell a safe adult. Being made whole often starts with one person who knows.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son To Where We Were Lying
truths.body: The man by the pool had thirty-eight years of nobody. Then Somebody came. God the Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ, and Jesus walked to that pool Himself and stood beside the man nobody carried. He saw him. He knew how long. Then He told him to rise, take up his bed and walk. Our Father did not wait for us to drag ourselves to the water. He sent His Son to where we were lying.

truths.title: Name What Keeps You Lying There
truths.body: Fathers, what keeps you lying by the pool? For some it is drink. For others it is betting, a phone, work, anger, or a woman who is not your wife: whatever makes the night shorter. Name it plainly to God; excuses keep a man lying there for years. Stopping is one night. Staying free is every night, and most men cannot do it alone. Find a pastor, a doctor, men who will ask you every week. Your children need a father who is free.

response.child: On a small paper, write the name your wound has given you. Cross it out. Under it, write your own name and: “God’s child.”
response.father: Name your habit out loud, to God, alone. Tell one person you trust about it this week.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: tonight speaks of habits such as drinking. Do not ask children to share their family story.
prayers: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, You see how long I have carried this. Yes, I want to be made whole.
Father, I will not make excuses tonight. Give me the help I cannot give myself.
Father, make our church a place where people who are stuck are carried.
days.declaration: My wound is not my name.

days.title: God Is Near The Broken-Hearted
days.verse: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
days.story: A boy found his sister sitting outside on the step at night. Then he remembered: she used to sing, and he had not noticed the day she stopped. Maybe someone you love has gone quiet. Maybe you have. Tonight we learn that God is near.
days.word: Read Psalm 34:15–18 aloud. David wrote this psalm after a time when he had to run for his life. The LORD’s eyes are on His people, and His ears are open to their cry. “Nigh” means near, close enough to touch. A “broken heart” is a heart that hurts too much to speak. A “contrite spirit” is truly sorry for wrong it has done. God does not wait for broken people to mend themselves before He comes close. Children, God is near the hurt and the quiet. Fathers, He is near the man who is truly sorry.

truths.title: God Notices When The Song Stops
truths.body: Maybe you used to sing, or laugh, or talk a lot, and somewhere along the way you went quiet, and nobody noticed. Grown-ups get busy. Brothers and sisters carry their own things. But God noticed. He knows the very day. Your quiet does not make you invisible to Him. If you are carrying something too heavy, you do not have to carry it alone: tell a safe adult. And if you wish you had noticed someone sooner, God does not ask you to carry that either. God is keeping every song safe.

truths.title: The Father Came Near In His Son
truths.body: “Nigh” means near. And God did not stay near only in His thoughts. The Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to come close to the broken-hearted: to people sitting outside in the dark, to the ones who have stopped singing. Jesus did not shout at sad people to cheer up. He noticed them and called them by name. He sat with them, and He stayed. That is how near the Father has come to you tonight.

truths.title: Notice, Then Stay
truths.body: Fathers, do you know whether your children still sing? Being away, or being too busy, means missing the small days too: the day a song stopped, the day it started again. Do not rush in and ask them to sing for you. You have not earned the song. Be honest with God that you do not know your own children as you should. And if you are in the house, look up. Notice. Then stay.

response.child: Hum one line of a song you love, even only to God. If a friend near you has gone quiet, sit beside them tomorrow.
response.father: Write down one thing you do not know about each of your children. Pray over each line.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story, or why anyone has gone quiet. Say slowly: “If somebody is hurting you: it is not your fault. Tell a safe adult. Keep telling until somebody believes you.” KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son, close to me. Keep my song safe.
Father, I was not there to notice, and You were. Teach me to notice and stay.
Father, make KIN a place where every quiet child is noticed.
days.declaration: God is near me. My song is safe.

days.title: When My Father’s Chair Is Empty
days.verse: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
days.story: At a full family table, a woman put a plate into a boy’s hands: “Your meat.” And the boy said, “In my father’s house, his chair was always empty. In this house, mine never was.” Maybe there is an empty chair in your home. Tonight we learn that the Father keeps a place for you.
days.word: Read Malachi 4:4–6 aloud. These are the last words of the Old Testament. God promises a messenger who will turn the hearts of fathers to their children. Not their feet: their hearts. A father can be in the house with his heart turned away. When fathers and children are turned from each other, a whole land suffers. After this, no new prophet spoke for about four hundred years. Then an angel repeated this promise (Luke 1:17), and the Father sent Jesus. Children, God cares about the empty chair in your home. Fathers, where is your heart turned tonight?

truths.title: The Empty Part Is In Him, Not In You
truths.body: Maybe your father lives far away. Or maybe he lives in your house and you are still looking for him: he sits in his chair but never asks what you learned today. That is a real sadness, and you may feel it. It is not because you are boring, or not clever enough, or not worth looking up for. The empty part is in him, not in you. And look around: people at church or at KIN may already be keeping a chair for you. Let them.

truths.title: The Father Did Not Stay In His Chair
truths.body: The Father showed us what a turned heart looks like. He sent Jesus Christ, His own Son, whose name is Emmanuel, which means God with us. Not God far away, watching something else. God with us: in the room, looking up. That is Christmas. The Father did not stay in His chair; He came, in His Son. At His table there is a place with your name on it. Nobody’s chair is empty because He forgot to look up.

truths.title: Look Up And Listen
truths.body: Some fathers never left. You are home every evening, and your children are still looking for you. Where is your heart turned: the screen, the phone, the business, yourself? You do not need a big speech. Ask your child to read to you, or to tell you one thing about their day, and listen with all of yourself. Ask where they go and who their friends are. One day, go with them. A father can be in the house and still need to come home.

response.child: Tomorrow, keep a seat for somebody who usually sits alone. Say their name when they sit down.
response.father: Put your phone in another room for one hour. Ask one child one question, and listen to the whole answer.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: some children’s fathers are home but far away; some are not home. Do not ask anyone to share their family story.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son, to be with me. You never look away from me.
Father, I have been in the room and not there; turn my heart to my children.
Father, let KIN keep a chair for every child.
days.declaration: My chair is never empty with God.

days.title: Fixing Home Is Not My Job
days.verse: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?
days.story: A boy of twelve thought the trouble at home was a money problem, so he went out to find money. He brought the coins to his mother and said, “Pay the rent yourself.” Many children try to fix what only grown-ups, with God’s help, can fix. Tonight we learn that wherever we go, our Father is already there.
days.word: Read Psalm 139:7–12 aloud. King David asks two questions, and he already knows the answer: nowhere. Up to heaven, down to the depths, across the sea, into the dark: God is there before him. “Whither” means where. “Flee” means run away. David is not frightened by this; it comforts him. Jonah tried to run from God by ship (Jonah 1:3), and God was there too. Children, there is no street, no market and no dark night where you are out of God’s reach. Fathers, you can run from a home, a family, a promise. You cannot run anywhere the Father is not already standing.

truths.title: You Do Not Have To Carry It
truths.body: Maybe home feels heavy: money is short, grown-ups are worried, and you want to help. The boy in the film thought it was a money problem, so he went to find money. But fixing home is not your job: not with money, not by working on the street, and not by running away. Those things are dangerous, and not everybody you meet is kind. Your job is to be a child. Tell a safe adult what is heavy: a teacher, a pastor, somebody at church. If one does not listen, tell another.

truths.title: The Father Came Into The Middle Of It
truths.body: When trouble comes, people often run, or try to fix it with money from far away. Look at how God the Father answered the biggest problem in the world. He did not send money through somebody. He sent His own Son, Jesus Christ, into the very place where we were. Jesus was born to a poor family and laid in a manger (Luke 2:7). That is Christmas: the Father did not run from the trouble. He came into the middle of it, and He is with you in yours tonight.

truths.title: Is Your Plan A Way Of Running?
truths.body: Fathers, is there a bag packed in your heart? A plan that sounds responsible: I will make money first, and come back when I have something to show. Is it a plan, or is it running? Your child does not need you to come back rich. Your child needs you to stop running: not to rush in, not to demand a welcome, but to stop hiding behind the money. A father should provide, but no amount of money can stand in for a father. Ask God honestly what you are running from.

response.child: If home feels heavy, write down the name of one safe adult you could tell. If you can, tell them this week.
response.father: Write down what you tell yourself you need before you can go back. Next to it: “My child needs a father, not this.”

days.teacherNote: Teacher: do not ask children to share their family story. If a child says they are thinking of running away, or are working to bring money home, follow your safeguarding procedure today.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son. When I want to run, remind me You are already there.
Father, I have been running and calling it something else. Unpack my bag.
Father, make our church people who go looking for every child who runs.
days.declaration: Wherever I go, my Father is already there.

days.title: Somebody Came Looking For Me
days.verse: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
days.story: A boy ran off alone, and somebody came after him. “How did you find me?” “I looked.” “Why?” “Because Somebody looked for me.” Maybe you have run, or hidden, or felt that nobody would bother to look for you. Tonight Jesus tells us He came looking on purpose.
days.word: Read Luke 19:1–10 aloud. Zacchaeus, a Jericho tax collector, was hated for taking more than he should. He climbed a tree to see Jesus. Jesus stopped under it, called him by name, and went to his house while the crowd grumbled. Zacchaeus did not clean himself up first; his life changed after Jesus came in. Then Jesus said why He had come: to seek and to save the lost. Lost does not mean worthless. It means far from home. Children, Jesus looks for you on purpose. Fathers, Jesus stops for the man everybody else has given up on.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son To Look
truths.body: God the Father did not wait for lost people to find their way home. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to look for them. Jesus told of a shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine and goes after one lost sheep “until he find it” (Luke 15:4). That is Christmas: the Father looking for us in His Son. He looks for the child who hides and for the man who has run. How did He find you? He looked.

truths.title: You Are Worth Looking For
truths.body: Maybe you feel lost, or hidden so well you think nobody would bother. Jesus came looking for you, not because you were good, but because you were lost, and He does not give up. Sometimes God sends safe people to sit beside you: a teacher, a pastor, an aunty. They are not God; like the man in the film, they look because Somebody looked for them first. Let them help you. If home feels heavy, tell one of them.

truths.title: Let Yourself Be Found
truths.body: Fathers, somebody may be looking for you: a pastor, a friend, a message you have not answered. You need not hide, or make a speech. You can say the honest thing: I have nothing to bring. Your child may not be waiting any more; that is their right, and you must respect it. But the first One looking for you is your Father in heaven, and He has been looking for a long time. Let Him find you tonight.

response.child: Think of another child who seems lonely at school or at church. Tomorrow, say good morning to them.
response.father: Answer one message you have been avoiding from somebody who has been looking for you. Not a speech. One honest line.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to look for me; when I hide, find me and bring me home.
Father, I have nothing to bring, but You sent Your Son to look for me, so here I am.
Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son; make our homes, our church and KIN places that look for the lost.
days.declaration: Jesus came looking for me.

days.title: Jesus Signed For Me
days.verse: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
days.story: A boy sat alone at a police station. The form asked for his father’s name, and nobody came to sign for him. Then one man said, “Whatever he owes, put it in my name,” because Somebody had signed for him. Maybe you feel you owe more than you can pay. Tonight we hear Who signed for us.
days.word: Read 2 Corinthians 5:17–21 aloud. Paul writes about coming back to God. Verse 17 says that anyone who is in Christ is made new: the old is gone. Verse 21 is a great exchange. Jesus “knew no sin”: He never did one wrong. On the cross God counted our sin against Jesus, so His goodness could be counted to us. Think of a form at a police station: the guilty one walks free because the innocent One signs. Children, this is for you, even on your worst day. Fathers, it is for you too, even with many years to answer for.

truths.title: The Father Sent His Son To Sign For Us
truths.body: Every one of us owes a debt we cannot pay. The Bible calls it sin. God our Father did not send a letter saying, “Try harder.” He sent His own Son, Jesus Christ, to the cross to sign for us. He took our wrong in His own name. The man in the film could sign for the boy only because Somebody had signed for him first. He was not the hero that day; he was pointing to Jesus.

truths.title: An Empty Line Is Not Your Name
truths.body: Maybe there is an empty line where your father’s name should be, or nobody came when you needed somebody. That empty line is not your name. If you have done wrong, and we all have, Jesus will sign for you; you need not be good first. Your Father in heaven knows your name, and He does not leave. When grown-ups fail you, it is not your fault. Tell a safe adult what you are carrying.

truths.title: Say It Without Excuses
truths.body: Fathers, maybe your child once needed somebody to stand for them, and it was not you. Say it plainly: That should have been me. Do not argue with it. A man who says it without excuses has started to come home. Thank God, without jealousy, for whoever stood in your place. Let Jesus Christ take your debt: the leaving, the money, the broken promises. Then put your own name on the small things your child needs.

response.child: Write your name on paper, and under it: Jesus signed for me. Keep it safe.
response.father: Thank God by name for one person who stood in your place for your child.

days.teacherNote: Say only what the film clip shows. Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, thank You that Jesus signed for me; an empty line is not my name.
Father, it should have been me; thank You that Jesus took my sin; make me stand for my child.
Father, thank You for Jesus Christ, Your Son; bless all who stand in the gap for children in our homes, our church and KIN.
days.declaration: Jesus signed for me, and He never leaves.

days.title: God Is My Safe Place
days.verse: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
days.story: In the film, safe grown-ups say what every child who tells needs to hear: “You did right to tell. It is not your fault. And you will not carry this alone for one more hour.” “I believe you. You are safe now.” Those words are for every child here. Tonight we learn that God is our safe place, and He sends safe people.
days.word: Read Psalm 46:1–7 aloud. It was sung when the whole world seemed to shake, yet the singers were not afraid: God was with them. A refuge is a safe place you can run into, like a strong house in a storm. “A very present help” means here, now, not later. Verse 7 says the Lord of armies is with us, and the God of Jacob is our fortress. Children, God is not far when a child is hurting; He is near, and on your side. Fathers, God protects children, and He calls every man here to be a safe man.

truths.title: God Is Here, And He Sent His Son
truths.body: When a child is hurt in secret, some think God must be far away. He is not. God our Father sent His Son, Jesus Christ, into a world where children get hurt. Jesus took little children in His arms and blessed them, and spoke His most serious words against anyone who harms a little one. He is on the child’s side. And He sends people, like the safe grown-ups in the film.

truths.title: It Is Not Your Fault. Tell
truths.body: If somebody is hurting you, it is not your fault, even if you were told to keep it secret, even if that person is family or somebody your family depends on. A secret that hurts you is not one you must keep. Tell a safe adult: a teacher, a pastor, an aunty. If the first does not listen, tell another. Keep telling until somebody believes you.

truths.title: Believe, Do Not Avenge
truths.body: Fathers, when a child tells, your part is smaller and harder than you think. Believe them. Do not ask for every detail, and do not take revenge; paying back belongs to God (Romans 12:19). Let the law and safe people do their work, and become a safe man. If you ever made a child afraid, their right to say no is not an insult; respect it. If you have hurt a child: stop, tell the truth, face the law.

response.child: Quietly, in your heart, name three safe adults you could tell if you needed to.
response.father: If you are with your child, say, “You can tell me anything, and I will believe you.” If not, pray for them by name.

days.teacherNote: Teacher: if a child tells you that someone is hurting them, thank them, believe them, do not question them in front of others, and follow your safeguarding procedure today. KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
prayers: Our Father, You are my safe place; give me courage to tell, and send somebody who believes.
Father, keep my children safe, and make me a safe man.
Father, thank You for Jesus Christ, Your Son; make our homes, our church and KIN safe for every child.
days.declaration: God is my refuge, and I will tell.

days.title: The People Who Show Up
days.verse: And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
days.story: In the film, ordinary men and helpers turn up to work. A boy is asked about a man in his life: “He is not your father. So what is he?” “My godfather. He is the one who introduced me.” The best people who show up do not take God’s place. They introduce us to Him.
days.word: Read Nehemiah 2:11–18 aloud. Jerusalem’s walls were broken down and its gates burnt. Nehemiah went out by night to see the damage. He told the people God’s good hand was on him, and they answered, “Let us rise up and build.” Strengthening their hands meant getting ready to work hard together. Chapter 3 shows who rebuilt the wall: not one rich man or a gift from far away, but ordinary families, each building the piece by their own house. Children, God uses small hands. Fathers, God still calls men to show up and build.

truths.title: The Son Of God Worked With His Hands
truths.body: God our Father did not send materials and a letter. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, a carpenter who worked with His hands. The Son of God knew dust and splinters; no worker is too low for Him, and no tired man is too far. Out of broken people, Jesus builds a family with God as its Father. He is the first of the ones who showed up.

truths.title: Small Pieces Are Enough
truths.body: Maybe your family feels like a broken wall, and you think you must fix it. You need not; you are a child. In Nehemiah’s day each family built one small piece. Your part can be small too: a kind word, a helping hand, one note of a song. If that is all you have tonight, it is enough. If you broke something, help mend it a little at a time, not so God will love you. He already does.

truths.title: Real Sorry Has Hands
truths.body: Fathers, you may owe a debt you can never pay: years, birthdays, school fees, promises you did not keep. Jesus has paid what you owe God. But real sorry has hands. Your children may need you to mend what can be mended, not with one big gift to make them forget; a gift cannot rebuild years. Like the helpers in the film, keep showing up, one ordinary day at a time, long after the gift is forgotten.

response.child: Mend one small thing, like a torn page or a loose button. Or hum one note of a song you love.
response.father: Write down one thing you broke that can still be mended, and one small, safe step to mend it.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for Jesus; help me build one small thing and mend one thing I broke.
Father, thank You for all who showed up for my children when I did not; make me a man who keeps showing up.
Father, thank You for Jesus Christ, Your Son, the first One who showed up; build our homes, our church and KIN.
days.declaration: We will be the ones who show up.

days.title: The Father Is Already In The Room
days.verse: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
days.story: In the film, a boy’s old watch has stopped. “This watch is not spoilt,” says a man. “It has just been on pause.” The boy cries, “Don’t touch it!” Some of us live on pause too, still waiting at a door. Tonight Jesus shows us that the Father is not far away. He is already in the room.
days.word: Read John 14:6–11 aloud. The night before the cross, Philip, after about three years with Jesus, still said, “Shew us the Father.” He was looking for the Father somewhere else, while the Father was showing Himself right in front of him. Jesus answered: whoever has seen Him has seen the Father. In verse 6 He says He is the way to the Father. Children, to know what our Father is like, look at Jesus: He touched people nobody would touch, took children in His arms, and forgave His enemies. Fathers, Jesus is not a messenger from a Father who stayed away. In Him, we see the Father.

truths.title: In Jesus, The Father Is In The Room
truths.body: Philip was looking past Jesus for the Father. Many of us do the same: we watch a door, the sky, a phone that does not ring. John wrote: “the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world” (1 John 4:14). The Father sent. The Son, Jesus Christ, came, all the way into the room. That is why anybody, even someone who has never prayed, can say, “God, good evening, it’s me,” and be heard.

truths.title: You Can Stop Watching The Door
truths.body: Maybe you lie awake, listening for a car, a step, a key in the door. Like the watch in the film, your heart may feel on pause. You can stop watching the door. Not because the person you wait for has come, or will come, but because Jesus is already in the room. You can pray, in these words or your own: Jesus, be my Father; be my life.

truths.title: Face Him Before You Face Your Child
truths.body: Fathers, maybe you have never prayed, or could not find the first word. Here is one: God. Two more: Good evening. Then say your name; He already knows it. You need not clean yourself up first. Tell Him the truth: I have nothing to bring. The Father sent the Son to save men who have nothing to bring. A man who has met God in the night walks differently into the next day.

response.child: Before sleep, say “Good evening” to God and tell Him one true thing about today.
response.father: Pray your first prayer, or your first honest one, out loud before midnight. Say your child’s name in it.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Jesus, be my Father; be my life; thank You for being already in the room.
God, good evening, it’s me; I have nothing to bring You; thank You for sending Your Son to save me.
Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son; teach our homes, our church and KIN to pray.
days.declaration: He is already in the room.

days.title: The Father Who Runs To Meet Us
days.verse: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
days.story: In the film, a father who has been away for years says, “I have nothing to bring that boy.” The answer comes: “He is not waiting for chicken any more.” And the boy’s old watch is working again. Maybe you think you have nothing to bring God. Tonight Jesus shows us a Father who runs to meet us.
days.word: Read Luke 15:11–24 aloud. Jesus told of a son who left home, wasted everything, and came back with nothing. While he was still far off, his father saw him and ran. A respected older man running down the road was not dignified, but this father did not care. He did not wait for a speech; he held his son, kissed him and threw a feast. Jesus was showing us what God our Father is like. No earthly father is perfect; this Father is. Children, God sees you from a great way off. Fathers, you too can come home to Him with nothing in your hands.

truths.title: The Father Ran, In His Son
truths.body: God our Father does not wait for us to reach the gate with something in our hands. He runs, and His running is Christmas. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, from heaven to a manger, and on to the cross, to reach us. An earthly father may come years late, or not at all. The Father sent His Son at the exact hour. The Father showed up.

truths.title: You Choose What Is Safe
truths.body: Maybe somebody will come back to your gate; maybe nobody will. If someone who left comes back, you need not run to him. Safe grown-ups should be around you and decide with you what is safe. Nobody may make you hug anybody, forgive in a hurry, or make a grown-up feel better. If he is not safe, he does not come close. And if nobody comes, the Father has already sent Jesus for you.

truths.title: Say “I Know” And Sit Where There Is Room
truths.body: Fathers, if you hope to go back, go the safe way: arranged through the safe adults around your child, to an open place, not the house. When your child says, “You are late,” say, “I know,” with no excuses. Sit where there is room, even on a children’s bench. Like the father in the film, you may feel you have nothing to bring; gifts are not the point. If your family is not ready, accept it. Come to the Father first. He saw you a great way off.

response.child: At eight tonight, look at a clock and say quietly: It is eight o’clock, and my Father is here.
response.father: At eight tonight, pray for your child by name. Any step back goes through the safe adults around your child, never by turning up unannounced.

days.teacherNote: Do not promise any child that a parent will come back. Do not ask children to share their own family story in the group.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for sending Jesus for me, right on time; whoever comes or does not come to my gate, You are my Father.
Father, I am late, and I know it; thank You for running to me in Your Son.
Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, Your Son; make our homes, our church and KIN places where every child has a chair.
days.declaration: It is eight o’clock, and my Father is here.

days.title: Christmas: The Father Gave His Son
days.verse: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
days.story: By lantern light, children heard tonight’s verse from Isaiah. Then their teacher told them God saw every child at every door. He did not send money through somebody. He came Himself, small, so the smallest child would not be afraid to come close. That is Christmas. The Father showed up, and He shows up for you.
days.word: Read Isaiah 9:2–7 aloud. Seven hundred years before Bethlehem, Isaiah spoke to people walking in darkness and promised them a great light: a child born, a son given. Stop on the word “given”. Not lent, not sold, not sent through somebody else. Given, as John 3:16 says: God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son. Then notice the strangest name in the verse: “The everlasting Father.” Who calls a baby “Father”? Isaiah did, because in the Son we see exactly what the Father is like. Christmas is not first about what we give each other. It is about what God gave us. Children, this gift is for you, whoever is at your table. Fathers, ask what you have given.

truths.title: The First Gift Was A Son
truths.body: On Christmas Day many of us think about gifts: new clothes, rice and stew, a toy, or the gift that never came. But the first gift of Christmas was not a thing. God our Father did not send a parcel from far away. He gave the One He loved most, Jesus Christ, His Son, and He gave Him to us. Jesus said, “he that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (John 14:9). Look at the baby in the manger, and see what your Father is like: He comes close.

truths.title: You Are On His List
truths.body: Maybe there was no father at your table this morning, or there was one and you wished there was not. God did not give His Son only to families with full tables.
