He gave Him to the world, and you are in the world. As the teacher in the film said, He came small, so that the smallest child would not be afraid to come close. You do not have to feel happy today to receive Him. And if somebody is hurting you, Christmas is not a reason to keep quiet. Tell a safe adult.

truths.title: Two Words Are A Place To Start
truths.body: Fathers, Christmas shows what a true father does: he comes himself. Maybe this year you sent nothing, or only sent money through somebody. Maybe you want to begin again and do not even know how to pray. Nobody is born knowing. Start with two words: “Our Father.” Then find a man who prays, sit beside him, and let him carry the prayer while you catch up. Do not ask your child to teach you or comfort you; that is not your child’s job.

response.child: Before you sleep, say “Our Father” slowly, out loud or in your heart, and thank Him for the gift of His Son and for one good thing from today.
response.father: Read the prayer that begins at Matthew 6:9, to the end, slowly. Then read Isaiah 9:6 again and thank God for His Son.

days.teacherNote: Christmas is hard for some children. Do not ask who was, or was not, at their table today.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for the first gift of Christmas, Your Son, Jesus Christ, given to me too.
Our Father: that is all I know, and I am starting there; teach me the rest.
Father, be close to every child at a full table tonight, and every child with none.
days.declaration: The Father gave His Son to me.

days.title: Fathers Who Learn To Pray
days.verse: And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
days.story: Children prayed “Our Father” in four languages. A boy said it clearly, and then saw that his own father could not say it. Nobody had ever taught him how. A teacher said, “We will start from there.” And the father whispered two words: “Our Father.” It is never too late to learn.
days.word: Read Deuteronomy 6:4–9 aloud. Moses is speaking to the whole people of God before they enter a new land. He gives fathers and mothers a job: talk about God at the table, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning. Faith is meant to be passed on in ordinary moments, not only in church. But look at the order. First the words are “in thine heart”. Then the parent teaches. A man cannot pour from an empty pot. Children, if nobody taught your father, that is not your job to fix; God can teach you Himself. Fathers, if your pot is empty, do not be ashamed. Begin with your own heart, and learn.

truths.title: The Father Sent A Teacher
truths.body: What does God do with a man who was never taught? He does not shout at him or shut the door. He sends a Teacher. God our Father sent Jesus Christ, His Son, to show us the Father and to teach us to talk to Him. When His friends asked Him to teach them to pray, He began with two words: “Our Father” (Luke 11:1–2). Perhaps nobody taught you. Now Somebody will. Jesus is patient with slow learners.

truths.title: It Is Not Your Job To Teach Your Father
truths.body: The Father in heaven teaches children Himself. You do not have to wait for a grown-up to go first. If your father cannot pray, or will not, that is not because of you, and it is not your job to fix him or carry him. Other grown-ups can help him. If he keeps saying “next week” about the things of God, you may be sad. Tell God. He is never “next week”. He is now.

truths.title: Sit On A Bench Of Praying Men
truths.body: Perhaps nobody taught you either. Men taught you to work hard, to make people laugh, or to leave, but nobody taught you to pray or to stay. The father in tonight’s film could manage only two words, and a teacher said, “We will start from there.” Start there too. Find men who pray, keep their word and share their bread. Say your one line, and let them carry the rest. And if your child asks you to come, do not say “next week”. Next week is a long time to a child.

response.child: Write “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name” (Matthew 6:9). Keep it where you sleep, and say it before you close your eyes.
response.father: Ask one man you respect, “Who taught you to pray?” Then ask if you can pray with him this week.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children who taught them to pray, or whose father prays. Let them answer in their hearts.
prayers: Our Father, thank You that nobody has to go first; You teach me Yourself.
Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name: thank You for Jesus Christ, Your Son, who teaches men like me.
Father, fill our benches with men who learn, pray and keep their word.
days.declaration: My Father in heaven teaches me Himself.

days.title: Forgiveness Does Not Mean Going Back
days.verse: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
days.story: A father came back seven years late. His son chose to forgive. The boy’s mother did not stand up, and she did not have to. The boy said, “Forgiving him was my own. Trusting him, he will have to earn.” Hear this tonight: forgiving is not trusting, and no child ever has to go back to anyone.
days.word: Read Ephesians 4:29–32 aloud. Paul is teaching Christians how to live together: no ugly words, no bitterness, no rage. Then he gives the reason we forgive: “even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” God did not forgive us by saying, “It does not matter.” It mattered so much that He gave His own Son to pay for it. Notice what Paul does not say. He does not say forgiving means pretending, forgetting or going back into danger. Proverbs 22:3 says a wise person sees danger coming and keeps away from it. Children, forgiving is a gift you may give when you are ready, even if you only tell God. Fathers, forgiveness is a gift. Trust is built.

truths.title: Forgiveness Is Never Pretending
truths.body: God our Father sent His only Son, Jesus Christ, to carry what we did wrong. The cross says two things at once: what was done was truly wrong, and My own Son will pay for it. That is how a hurting person can forgive without pretending. We were forgiven first, by the Father who sent His Son for us. You never have to earn that forgiveness. Tonight it is yours. And because it is yours, one day you can give it away without ever calling wrong right.

truths.title: Forgiving Is Not Going Back
truths.body: Maybe somebody told you a good Christian child must forgive and forget, and go back. That is not what the Bible says. You may forgive in your heart and still stay far away. You may forgive and still tell a safe adult. No child ever has to make peace with, visit, or go back to anyone. You never have to make a grown-up feel better about what they did. The boy in the film said trust would have to be earned; that is wise. If you are not ready to forgive yet, tell God. He is patient.

truths.title: Trust Is Earned, Not Demanded
truths.body: Fathers, if you have come back, go to the back of the line. Do not ask anyone to say it is all right. Do not ask your child to forgive you, hug you or speak up for you. If you were violent in your home, coming back means getting help first: a pastor, a counsellor, men who will hold you to account. Let the mother and other safe adults decide what is safe. Trust is not owed to you; it is earned. Keep your word, small and steady, for as long as it takes.

response.child: On a private paper write “Forgive” and a name, or “not yet”. Under it write “Safe” and a grown-up you can tell anything.
response.father: Keep one small promise this week, only where you are welcome and it is safe, without announcing it. Let your family count.

days.teacherNote: Never ask a child whom they must forgive, or to forgive aloud. If a child says someone is hurting them, believe them and follow your safeguarding procedure. KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
prayers: Our Father, thank You for forgiving me through Jesus; help me forgive when I am ready, and keep me safe.
Father, thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, to forgive me; teach me to earn trust one day at a time.
Father, make our homes and KIN places where no child is rushed and every child is safe.
days.declaration: I can forgive and still be safe.

days.title: I Am Not An Orphan
days.verse: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
days.story: In the film, a family found a new home. A woman gave a girl her own daughter’s bed, and nobody asked them how long they would stay. That is what it feels like to be taken in. Jesus made a promise like that to His friends: I will not leave you as orphans. I will come to you.
days.word: Read John 14:15–21 aloud. It is the night before Jesus died. He tells His frightened friends that He is going away, and they feel they are about to be left alone. Then He makes this promise. In the Greek John wrote in, the word we read as “comfortless” is the word for orphans. Jesus is saying: I will not leave you fatherless. He promises the Holy Spirit to be with them for ever, and He promises to come Himself. Children, you are not an orphan, whoever is or is not in your house tonight. Fathers, notice that Jesus did not say “we will see” or “next week”. He said, “I will come.”

truths.title: The Son Keeps His Word
truths.body: This promise came from the Son whom the Father sent, and He kept it. God our Father sent Jesus Christ, His Son, to bring us home to Himself. Jesus rose again and sent His Spirit, just as He said. So a child whose father keeps saying “we will see” is not an orphan. The Father in heaven already came, in Jesus. God is not “next week”. God is not “we will see”. He came, and He stays.

truths.title: You Are Still Fathered
truths.body: Maybe your father is at home but always on his phone, always saying “next week”. Maybe he is far away, or gone. That hurts, and you may tell God so. It is not because you are not good enough. A child who wants his father is not asking for too much. Now look around. Who sets a plate in front of you? Who makes room for you, like the woman in the film who gave a girl her own daughter’s bed? They are not the Father. They are His hands, showing you He is real.

truths.title: At Home Is Not The Same As There
truths.body: Fathers, some men left. Some never left and were still not there. If your child keeps asking you to come and see, and you keep saying “next week”, hear this: your child is keeping a chair for you. Every time you do not come, a little more of them stops looking at the gate. Put the phone down. Turn up where you were asked. And thank God for every person who made room for your children when you did not.

response.child: Think of one person who kept a place for you this year, and thank God for them by name.
response.father: If you are at home tonight, turn off your phone and sit with your child for ten minutes. Ask one question, and listen to the whole answer.

days.teacherNote: Some children have a father at home who is not there. Do not ask children to describe their fathers.
prayers: Lord Jesus Christ, God’s Son, thank You that I am not an orphan; sit with me when my chair feels empty.
Father, You did not say “next week” to me; You sent Your Son. Make me a man who comes.
Father, let no child at our tables sit beside an empty chair alone.
days.declaration: I am not an orphan. I am still fathered.

days.title: God Stepped Into Our Time
days.verse: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
days.story: A boy sat facing a door, holding a watch he had stopped years ago, still waiting for a father. His teacher said the watch had only kept him five years old. Then the boy prayed, “Jesus. Be my Father. Be my life.” He had been watching the door. God was already in the room.
days.word: Read Psalm 90:12–17 aloud. This psalm is a prayer of Moses, who had seen many years of trouble in the wilderness. He asks God to teach us to count our days well, and to give us gladness for as many years as we have seen sorrow. Hurt can make us stop counting. Part of us stays the age we were when something went wrong, waiting at the same door. Numbering our days means receiving each one from the Father as a gift, and letting time move again. Children, your clock can move again; God can give gladness for sad years. Fathers, you cannot get back the years you lost, but today is the day you have.

truths.title: The Son Came Into Our Time
truths.body: God did not stop time, and He did not stay outside it. He came into it. When the time was right, God our Father sent Jesus Christ, His Son, into the world (Galatians 4:4). He was born on a real day, in a real town, and grew up one day at a time, like you. The Son came into our time so that our time could move again. Whatever door you have been watching, He is already in the room.

truths.title: Your Story Belongs To You
truths.body: Maybe something happened that stopped a clock inside you, and part of you is still that age. Jesus is with you in this minute, not only in that one. If you want to tell your story, tell a safe adult first. You never have to tell it to the person who hurt you, and you never have to make them feel better. Telling is your choice, and so is when. Like the boy in the film, you can give that stopped clock to Jesus tonight and ask Him to be your Father.

truths.title: Sorry With No “But”
truths.body: Fathers, one day your child may tell you what it was like when you were not there. If that day comes, listen. Do not defend yourself or tell your own sad story. Listen to the end. Say “I am sorry” with no “but”. Say “Thank you for telling me.” If your child never wants to tell you, do not chase the story or push for a talk. That choice belongs to them. Keep your word quietly, and let the years show the change.

response.child: Whisper to God, “I give You the clock I stopped.” You may tell a safe adult anything that hurts.
response.father: Write “I am sorry”, with no “but”, and what for. If it is safe and wanted, give it one day. If not, give it to God tonight.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share family stories. If a child tells you privately that someone is hurting them, believe them and follow your safeguarding procedure. KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
prayers: Our Father, I give You the clock I stopped; thank You that Jesus Christ, Your Son, is with me in this minute.
Father, I cannot give back the years I took; teach me to listen, and to say sorry with no “but”.
Father, make our homes and churches places where children are believed and kept safe.
days.declaration: My time is moving, and Jesus is with me.

days.title: If You Have No Father, You Do Now
days.verse: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
days.story: On the last night, a boy said some of his friends’ fathers never came back. The real miracle was this: “I have a Father. He has never been late. His name is Jesus.” If somebody is hurting you, it is not your fault: tell a safe adult. And if you have no father, you do now.
days.word: Read 1 John 5:9–13 aloud. John was an old man writing to Christians he loved, and he tells them why he wrote: so that they may know they have eternal life. Not hope, not guess: know. God has given us life, and this life is in His Son. Then the key line: “He that hath the Son hath life.” Not “he that hath a father who came back”. Not “he that hath a happy Christmas”. He that hath the Son. So the child whose father never came is not shut out, and the father who came late is not shut out either. Children and fathers, this life is for you tonight, whatever happened at your door.

truths.title: If You Have No Father, You Do Now
truths.body: This is the last night of these thirty days, not the last night of your story. Maybe your father came back. Maybe he never will. Maybe he is in the house and still not there. If somebody is hurting you, it is not your fault. Tell a safe adult, and keep telling until somebody believes you. And if you have no father, you do now: God is your Father. He has never been late. Give Him whatever you have been holding onto while you waited at the door.

truths.title: Come Home To Him First
truths.body: Fathers, perhaps you are still far away from your children. Coming back may take a long time, and it may only be right to come slowly, where you are welcome and it is safe. Keep your word every day, like everybody else, with no shortcuts. But remember what comes first. You cannot give your child what you have never received. Come home to the Father first, on your knees, tonight. Then let Him teach you how to be a father, one honest step at a time.

truths.title: In The Son We See The Father
truths.body: God is our Father, and He sent Jesus Christ, His Son. The Father sent the Son, and in the Son we see exactly what the Father is like. Jesus said, “he that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (John 14:9). Isaiah calls the Son “The everlasting Father” (Isaiah 9:6). So we can say it: Jesus Christ is the Father, and He is my life.

response.child: Write on a paper: “I have a Father. He has never been late. His name is Jesus.”
response.father: If you are with your child and it is safe and welcome, say the blessing in Numbers 6:24–26 over them. If not, pray it over their name.

days.teacherNote: Do not ask children to share their family stories. If a child tells you someone is hurting them, believe them and follow your safeguarding procedure. KIN line: +234 812 267 3417.
prayers: Jesus, God’s Son, I have a Father; You have never been late. Be my Father. Be my life.
Our Father, thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, for me and my children; I receive Him.

Over every child and every home: “The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.” — Numbers 6:24–26
days.declaration: Jesus Christ is the Father, and He is my life.

closing.title: Jesus Christ is the Father
closing.declaration: JESUS CHRIST IS THE FATHER. AND HE IS YOUR LIFE.
closing.quote: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given … and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” — Isaiah 9:6 (KJV, excerpt)
